label: input token n during the original phase
explanation: Fires whenever the input token is n during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase, at any position and any L; precision 1.0 and ~98% recall on dev. Does not fire on n when it is fed back as input in the copy phase, nor on the delimiter step, nor on any other token except rare weak activations on j (0.3% of mass). Magnitude is fairly uniform (median ~0.78 of max); repeated occurrences of n in a sequence tend to activate somewhat more weakly than the first occurrence (examples show 0.6-0.8 vs ~0.85), and top activations tend to be late-position n in sequences that begin with d or 3.

issues: On the test split, every original-phase n is active (0 false positives, precision 1.0, recall 0.985, F1 0.992, mass recall 0.997). The firing does not depend on phase, L, to_go or orig_idx: the rate on n stays about flat at 0.033-0.037 per position.
The claims about the delimiter and copy phase hold: dev shows 0 activations on the delimiter step and 1 in the copy phase.

All the missed activations are weak j activations (relative activation 0.13-0.21) holding 0.3% of the mass. That is the exception the explanation already states. Adding j to the predicate (j at t>=5) drops test precision to 0.81 and F1 to 0.89, so the j firing is too sparse to count as a real second meaning.

The magnitude claims (repeat occurrences of n fire more weakly, the strongest activations come on late-position n) were only checked against the example sequences. The explanation admits this. They are minor and do not affect the label.
